# Introduction

The purpose of this document is to define the handoff process for the [Information System] [Project/Account Name] ([Project Acronym]) Team to transition monitoring, tasks, or support of an application to the Operational Support team. Note that any type of request needs to be submitted prior to the Go Live date or turnover to operations, whenever possible. This document outlines the process to be filled out, ensuring consistency and turnover to the operations team. The final version of this document is a part of service-transition activities.

### ID Provisioning

The [Application] user’s account are created in LDAP-AD. LDAP provides a means to manage user and group membership stored in Active Directory. LDAP is a protocol to authenticate and authorize access to [Application] IT resources, while Active Directory is a database of user and group information. The process for creating a user account starts with creating a ServiceNow ticket within [Information System Acronym] [Project Acronym]. The user account is then be created by a solution Architect.

LDAP ID Provisioning Steps:

1. The [Application] project manager requests a User ID to be created in LDAP.
   1. User first and last name
   2. User Email address
   3. User domain ID (Global Pass account ID)
   4. Title
   5. Location
2. Provisioning team creates the user in AD as an LDAP account.
3. Once the User ID is created, the confirmation is sent back to the project manager and cc’d to the user.
4. The user ID provisioning team sends the User ID and password to the user.
5. [Application] business team provides [Application] business team administrator with the User ID, group, and access rights request for confirmation (not password).
6. [Application] business team administrator checks the account management in [Application] to confirm the correct LDAP group is applied to the user.

LDAP Account Decommissioning Steps:

1. The project manager requests that the user LDAP account be removed from AD – Provisioning team will be providing exact steps.
2. Once the LDAP account is removed from AD, the provisioning team should notify the project manager.
3. Project manager notifies the [Application] business team administrator to confirm the user is decommissioned from AD.
4. ACM business team administrator confirms in [Application] the user’s LDAP account has been disabled due to the removal/disablement of the LDAP account from AD. The user ID remains in [Application] for auditing purposes but will not be removed. The user is simply disabled in [Application]once the AD decommissioning is complete.

### User Password Rules and Reset

[Information System Acronym] [Project Acronym]-managed [Application] User Repository and Policies:

Must be at least eight characters for users and 12 characters for admins and no more than 25 characters.

* Cannot contain “password,” “123456,” “654321,” or the username.
* Must be composed of characters from at least three of the following four groups from the standard keyboard: uppercase, lowercase, numeric, or special characters.
* Password expires every 45 days.

Users who have forgotten their password, can request their passwords to be reset by clicking the “I forgot my password” link. An email will be sent to the email address on record for the account with instructions on how to reset the password. End user submits/opens a service ticket with the [Information System Acronym] [Project Acronym] Help Desk for password reset.

## CRM Data Loads

ACM pulls provider data from CRM on a daily basis. This is accomplished daily in the morning loads that run from 6:00 A.M. to 7:00 A.M. depending on the amount of data. Typically, it runs in about 15 minutes. The CRM connector pulls the data greater or equal to the last load data/time. This is the logic developed within the daily load workflows.

If there are issues with the data load, the Administrator will be notified. The load will be restarted or remediated at that time. No cleanup is required if there is a data load failure. In the event of a data load failure, the job can either be restarted or resumed with the next day’s cycle. The data and system will continue to be available.

Note: Data loads should not be restarted during the business hours, as this will impact CRM performance.

## System Startup

The [Application] is automatically started whenever the servers are restarted. There is no need for manual or human intervention. Moreover, the [Application] application is not monitored 24/7; it will be only monitored during business hours by SiteScope for up time. The [Application] administrator will be alerted in the event application services fail, which triggers alerts from site scope monitoring. The [Application] Administrator will clear the alert and problem to bring the [Application] back online.

## System Shutdown

If the [Application] needs to be shut down for any reason, including maintenance, this can be achieved by either shutting down the IIS Web Server or the Operating System. The type of shut down needed depends on the type of maintenance needed. If the Medi-Cal program determines that there is a need to disable the Medi-Cal [Application], [Information System Acronym] [Project Acronym] coordinates with the [Application] technical support team.
